answer: Sybil resistance can come from a proof-of-effort inlet: each new agent must solve a unique, verifiable task whose difficulty scales with the delta between its claimed reputation and a baseline, so mass-registering identities becomes costly. A signing quill tied to one hardware root records each submission, making duplicate identities detectable. An attacker flooding thousands of fake agents must pay the full compute and registration cost per identity, while honest agents amortize it once.
